title.ja: Data Movement: DataSync、Data Pipeline のいま、データを運ぶ手段の選び方
title.en: Data Movement: DataSync, Data Pipeline Today, and Choosing How to Move Data

sources.title: What is AWS Data Pipeline?
supports: AWS Data Pipeline is no longer available to new customers; existing customers can continue to use the service as normal
The service is in maintenance mode and no new features or region expansions are planned
A pipeline definition specifies the business logic, a pipeline schedules and runs tasks by creating Amazon EC2 instances, and Task Runner polls for tasks and performs them
Tasks can be dependent on the successful completion of previous tasks

sources.title: Migrating workloads from AWS Data Pipeline
supports: Typical Data Pipeline use cases can be migrated to AWS Glue, AWS Step Functions, or Amazon MWAA
Step Functions is recommended for a serverless orchestration service that charges per task execution and orchestrates other AWS services
The concept table maps pipelines to workflows, activities to states and tasks, attempts to catchers and retriers, and the pipeline schedule to EventBridge Scheduler
Glue is recommended when the pipeline came from a console template such as exporting a DynamoDB table to S3; MWAA when workflows are written in Python on Apache Airflow

sources.title: Migrate workloads from AWS Data Pipeline (AWS Big Data Blog)
supports: New customer access to AWS Data Pipeline was closed effective July 25, 2024
Existing customers can continue to use the service as normal
sources.note: Read through a fetch tool that returned excerpts. No end-of-support date is stated on this page or on the two guide pages.

sources.title: AWS Data Pipeline: Pipeline Definition, Activities, Data Nodes, Preconditions, Resources
supports: A pipeline definition contains data sources, activities, their schedule, the resources that run them, preconditions, and ways to alert
Activity types include CopyActivity, EmrActivity, HiveActivity, ShellCommandActivity, and SqlActivity
Data nodes include S3DataNode, DynamoDBDataNode, SqlDataNode, and RedshiftDataNode; resources are Ec2Resource and EmrCluster
A precondition must be true before an activity can run, for example S3KeyExists
sources.note: Also read: dp-concepts-activities.html, dp-concepts-datanodes.html, dp-concepts-preconditions.html, dp-concepts-resources.html in the same guide.

sources.title: What is AWS DataSync?
supports: DataSync is a file transfer service for file or object data to, from, and between AWS storage services
The other clouds it lists include Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, and Cloudflare R2 Storage
DataSync includes encryption in transit and data integrity validation

sources.title: How AWS DataSync transfers work
supports: An agent is a VM appliance; a location is where data is copied from or to; a task describes a transfer; a task execution is one run of it
By default DataSync prepares a transfer by scanning both locations to find differences; with transfer-all it does not compare
DataSync always performs integrity checks during a transfer and can verify again at the end
A file written to during a transfer can be detected at verification, and getting its latest version needs another run
Transfers between AWS storage services in one account need no agent and stay on the AWS network

sources.title: Choosing a task mode for your data transfer
supports: Enhanced mode lists, prepares, transfers, and verifies in parallel and works with virtually unlimited numbers of objects; Basic mode does these sequentially and is subject to quotas
Enhanced mode verifies only transferred data; Basic mode verifies all data by default
Enhanced mode logs are structured JSON; Basic mode logs are unstructured
The task mode cannot be changed after the task is created
Creating an Enhanced mode task needs iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole

sources.title: Where can I transfer my data with AWS DataSync?
supports: S3 to S3 needs no agent in Basic and Enhanced mode, within one account and across accounts
Other cloud storage to S3 needs an agent only in Basic mode; NFS and SMB always need an agent
Between AWS storage services in different Regions, one of the two locations must be in the Region where DataSync is used
Data transferred between Regions is billed as data transfer out from the source Region to the destination Region

sources.title: Do I need an AWS DataSync agent?
supports: An agent is needed between AWS storage and on-premises storage, and between EFS or FSx and other clouds
No agent is needed between AWS storage services in the same account, or between S3 and object storage in other clouds

sources.title: Configuring AWS DataSync transfers with Amazon S3
supports: The IAM permissions a source location role and a destination location role need, action by action
New objects get the storage class of the destination location; existing objects keep theirs unless the task transfers all data
In a versioned bucket DataSync creates a new version when the source object is modified, and only the latest version of a source object is transferred
DataSync makes LIST, HEAD, GET, PUT, and COPY requests on every run, HEAD requests even when nothing moves

Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, and Glacier Instant Retrieval can charge for overwriting, deleting, or retrieving, and objects under 128 KB are stored in S3 Standard instead; archived objects must be restored before DataSync can read them
A bucket encrypted with SSE-C cannot be accessed; SSE-KMS needs the role in the key policy

sources.title: Tutorial: Transferring data between Amazon S3 buckets across AWS accounts
supports: The DataSync role, both locations, and the task are created in the source account
The destination bucket's policy names that role and allows ten S3 actions on the bucket and its objects
ACLs are disabled on the destination bucket so that its account owns the objects
A cross-account location cannot be created in the console; create-location-s3 is run with the destination bucket's Region
To avoid a network connection error the task is created in the same Region as the destination location; with Basic mode across accounts and Regions the alternative is an Enhanced mode task

sources.title: DataSync API: Options
supports: TransferMode CHANGED (default) or ALL; OverwriteMode ALWAYS (default) or NEVER; PreserveDeletedFiles PRESERVE (default) or REMOVE
VerifyMode ONLY_FILES_TRANSFERRED, POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT (default for Basic mode, not supported in Enhanced mode), or NONE
ObjectTags PRESERVE (default) or NONE; LogLevel OFF, BASIC, or TRANSFER
OverwriteMode NEVER protects against overwriting changes made in the destination

sources.title: Configuring how to handle files, objects, and metadata
supports: A task cannot both delete data in the destination and transfer all data, because transfer-all does not scan the destination
Deleting or overwriting objects can incur minimum storage duration, retrieval, or early deletion charges in some storage classes

sources.title: Understanding how DataSync handles file and object metadata
supports: Between object storage and Amazon S3, DataSync copies user-defined metadata, object tags, and Content-Disposition, Content-Encoding, Content-Language, and Content-Type
DataSync does not copy object ACLs, prior object versions, or the Last-Modified key
sources.note: The table row is headed 'Object storage, Amazon S3'. The page has no row that names S3 to S3 separately.

sources.title: Configuring how AWS DataSync verifies data integrity
supports: During a transfer DataSync uses checksum verification; verification at the end is an additional, configurable step
Verify-all checks the entire source and destination at the end and cannot be used with Enhanced mode or with Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive destinations

sources.title: Transferring specific files, objects, and folders by using filters
supports: A filter is patterns joined by a pipe; filters are case sensitive and relative to the source location path
/dir and /dir/ both match the folder and its content, and a slash in an S3 key is treated as a folder
Include filters support the wildcard only as the rightmost character of a pattern
A backslash escapes *, | and \
sources.note: The page does not say whether a destination object that a filter excludes is deleted when deleted files are removed.

sources.title: Transferring specific files or objects by using a manifest
supports: A manifest is a CSV file listing the exact files or objects to transfer, optionally with an S3 version ID
A manifest cannot be combined with filters, and DataSync deletes nothing in the destination when one is used
The maximum manifest size with Enhanced mode is 20 GB

sources.title: Scheduling when your AWS DataSync task runs
supports: A task schedule is a cron or rate expression with a minimum interval of one hour
DataSync may disable a schedule when the task fails repeatedly with the same error; the schedule's Status, DisabledBy, and DisabledReason show it

sources.title: Starting a task to transfer your data
supports: Task execution statuses are QUEUED, LAUNCHING, LAUNCHED, PREPARING, TRANSFERRING, VERIFYING, SUCCESS, CANCELLING, and ERROR
start-task-execution starts a run and can override options for that run

sources.title: Monitoring your data transfers with task reports
supports: Task reports are JSON files about what DataSync attempted to transfer, skip, verify, and delete, as a summary or with per-object lists
A task report is written to an S3 bucket named in the task report configuration
sources.note: The destination is read from API_TaskReportConfig.html.

sources.title: Monitoring data transfers with Amazon CloudWatch Logs
supports: An Enhanced mode task logs to the log group /aws/datasync, created through a service-linked role
A Basic mode task logs to a group named by CloudWatchLogGroupArn, which needs a CloudWatch Logs resource policy for datasync.amazonaws.com with CreateLogStream and PutLogEvents

sources.title: Monitoring events by using Amazon EventBridge
supports: DataSync emits events for agent, location, task, and task execution state changes on a best-effort basis
Task execution states include Success and Error

sources.title: EventBridge events reference: AWS DataSync
supports: The source is aws.datasync and the detail types include DataSync Task Execution State Change
Delivery is best effort

sources.title: AWS Knowledge Center: email notifications for DataSync task execution status
supports: A sample event carries the task execution ARN in resources and detail.State with the value SUCCESS
An event pattern that matches detail.State SUCCESS or ERROR, optionally with a prefix match on the execution ARN in resources
sources.note: Marked AWS OFFICIAL. The sample's ARN is written arn:aws:sync:...; the patterns on the same page use arn:aws:datasync:.... The spellings of other states in detail.State are not shown.

sources.title: AWS DataSync quotas
supports: 100 tasks per account and Region (adjustable)
Basic mode between AWS storage services: 25 million files, objects, and directories per execution, with S3 prefixes counted as directories; 50 million with on-premises or other clouds
Enhanced mode: virtually unlimited objects per execution, 120 concurrent executions
Filters up to 102,400 characters; 50 queued executions per task; execution history kept 30 days; S3 object names up to 1,024 UTF-8 characters

sources.title: Cross-service confused deputy prevention (DataSync)
supports: A trust policy for datasync.amazonaws.com with aws:SourceAccount and an aws:SourceArn of the form arn:aws:datasync:<region>:<account>:*

sources.title: Configuring transfers with other cloud object storage
supports: Cloudflare R2 is reached at <account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com as an object storage location
Transfers between other clouds' object storage and S3 in Enhanced mode need no agent
Copying object tags can fail with providers that do not support them

sources.title: AWS DataSync pricing
supports: A flat per-gigabyte fee for data transferred; Enhanced mode tasks are also charged a fee per task execution
There are no upfront costs and no minimum charges
S3 LIST, HEAD, GET, PUT, and COPY requests, data transfer between Regions, and CloudWatch Logs are charged at their standard rates
sources.note: Read through a fetch tool that returned excerpts. The page does not say whether an execution that copies nothing, fails, or is cancelled is charged the per-execution fee.

supports: DataSync has endpoints in ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo) and ap-northeast-3 (Osaka)

sources.title: AWS::DataSync::Task and AWS::DataSync::LocationS3
supports: The task's properties include SourceLocationArn, DestinationLocationArn, TaskMode (BASIC or ENHANCED, replacement on change), Options, Schedule, Includes, Excludes, and CloudWatchLogGroupArn
LocationS3 takes S3BucketArn, S3Config.BucketAccessRoleArn, S3StorageClass, and Subdirectory

sources.title: Resource types that support Cloud Control API
supports: AWS::DataSync::LocationS3, AWS::DataSync::Task, and AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy support create, read, update, delete, and list

sources.title: @go-to-k/cdkd 0.296.28: bundled dist (provider registry)
supports: Dedicated providers are registered for AWS::S3::Bucket, AWS::S3::BucketPolicy, AWS::IAM::Role, AWS::IAM::Policy, AWS::Lambda::Function, AWS::Lambda::Permission, AWS::Logs::LogGroup, AWS::Events::Rule, AWS::SNS::Topic, and AWS::SNS::TopicPolicy

A non-empty bucket is not deleted unless it opted into automatic emptying

sources.title: Replicating objects within and across Regions
supports: Live replication copies new and updated objects automatically and asynchronously, and does not replicate objects that existed before it was set up
S3 Batch Replication replicates existing objects on demand
S3 Replication Time Control replicates 99.99 percent of new objects within 15 minutes

sources.title: Requirements and considerations for replication
supports: Both source and destination buckets must have versioning enabled

sources.title: Amazon S3 API: Object (ETag)
supports: An ETag is an MD5 digest of the object data only for objects created by PUT, POST, or Copy with SSE-S3 or no encryption; for multipart uploads it is not

sources.title: How Lambda handles errors and retries with asynchronous invocation
supports: When a function invoked asynchronously returns an error, Lambda by default runs it two more times
EventBridge event buses and rules invoke Lambda asynchronously
sources.note: The second claim is from lambda-services.html in the same guide.

sources.title: What is Amazon S3? (data consistency model)
supports: Updates to a single key are atomic: a concurrent GET returns the old data or the new data, never partial or corrupt data
There is no way to make atomic updates across keys

sources.title: Performing object operations in bulk with Batch Operations
supports: A job performs one operation, such as copy, on every object in a manifest, which can come from an S3 Inventory report
S3 tracks progress and stores a completion report

sources.title: AWS CLI: s3 sync
supports: sync recursively copies new and updated files from the source to the destination, between a local directory and S3 or between two S3 URIs
--delete removes files that exist in the destination but not in the source, except those excluded by filters

sources.title: What is AWS Transfer Family?
supports: Transfer Family offers managed SFTP, AS2, FTPS, FTP, and browser-based transfers into and out of S3 and EFS

sources.title: What is Snowball Edge?
supports: AWS Snowball Edge is no longer available to new customers, who are pointed to DataSync for online transfers and AWS Data Transfer Terminal for physical ones
sources.note: Only the notice on this page was read. Other Snow family devices and Data Transfer Terminal's own pages were not checked.

sources.title: What is AWS Database Migration Service?
supports: DMS migrates relational databases, data warehouses, and NoSQL databases, as a one-time migration or by replicating ongoing changes

sources.title: What is Amazon Data Firehose?
supports: Firehose delivers real-time streaming data to destinations such as Amazon S3

sources.title: Cloudflare R2: Super Slurper
supports: Super Slurper copies objects from other cloud providers, including Amazon S3, into an R2 bucket as a one-off bulk job
Objects in Glacier tiers other than Instant Retrieval are skipped, and objects over 1 TB are skipped
ETags may differ after migration
sources.note: Read through a fetch tool that returned excerpts.

sources.title: Cloudflare R2: Sippy
supports: Sippy copies an object from the source bucket to R2 the first time it is requested, while returning it to the client
Later modifications to the object in the source are not reflected in R2
sources.note: Read through a fetch tool that returned excerpts.

sources.title: Cloudflare R2: Pricing
supports: Egress (data transfer to the internet) is free
Standard storage is USD 0.015 per GB-month; Class A operations USD 4.50 and Class B USD 0.36 per million
Super Slurper is charged only for the Class A operations it makes on the R2 bucket
sources.note: Read through a fetch tool that returned excerpts.

definition.ja: DataSync がコピーの元か先として扱う置き場所の登録。S3 なら、バケットと、DataSync がそのバケットに届くためのロールの組。作るだけでは何も動かない。
definition.en: A storage place registered with DataSync as somewhere to copy from or to. For S3 it is a bucket together with the role DataSync uses to reach it. Creating one runs nothing.

definition.ja: ソースとデスティネーションのロケーション、コピーのしかたの設定、スケジュールをまとめたもの。ECS のタスクとは別のもの。
definition.en: A source location, a destination location, the options for how to copy, and a schedule, as one resource. Not related to an ECS task.

definition.ja: DataSync のタスクを 1 回動かしたもの。準備、転送、検証の段階を進み、SUCCESS か ERROR で終わる。
definition.en: One run of a DataSync task. It goes through preparing, transferring, and verifying, and ends in SUCCESS or ERROR.

definition.ja: 自分のネットワークの中に置く仮想マシンで、DataSync の代わりに NFS や SMB のストレージを読み書きする。S3 どうしのコピーには要らない。
definition.en: A virtual machine placed in your own network that reads and writes NFS or SMB storage on DataSync's behalf. A copy between two S3 buckets needs none.

definition.ja: 権限を持つサービスが、別の誰かの依頼で、依頼した人には触れないはずのリソースを操作してしまう問題。信頼ポリシーに `aws:SourceAccount` と `aws:SourceArn` の条件を書いて防ぐ。
definition.en: A service with permissions being talked into acting on a resource its caller could not touch. Prevented with `aws:SourceAccount` and `aws:SourceArn` conditions in the trust policy.

ja: 添付は 10,000 個で合計 10 GB。キーは 07章の形（`u/<owner>/<note>/<attachment>`）で、所有者 100 人、ノート 1,000 件。フォルダーにあたるプレフィックスは 1,101 個
実行は 1 回で、全部をコピーする。Basic モード
リクエストの数は仮定。ソース側は LIST 1,101、HEAD 10,000、GET 10,000、タグの GET 20,000。アーカイブ側は LIST 1,101、PUT 10,000、検証の HEAD 10,000。1 個は 1 回の PUT で書かれるとした
リージョン間のデータ転送は、ソースのリージョンから出る料金として数えた

en: 10,000 attachments, 10 GB in all, with chapter 07's keys (`u/<owner>/<note>/<attachment>`): 100 owners and 1,000 notes, so 1,101 prefixes that count as folders
One execution in Basic mode that copies everything

The request counts are assumptions. Source: 1,101 LIST, 10,000 HEAD, 10,000 GET, 20,000 tagging GET. Archive: 1,101 LIST, 10,000 PUT, 10,000 HEAD for verification. Each object is taken to be written with one PUT
Data transfer between Regions is counted as transfer out of the source Region
Archive storage is 10 GB in S3 Standard for one month

note.ja: 63 件。計画（新規・変更・同じ、PRESERVE と REMOVE、ソースの一覧が空のときの全削除、フィルターで外したものは削除しない、アーカイブ側が新しいオブジェクトの上書きと OverwriteMode NEVER、TransferMode ALL、include と exclude、ALL と REMOVE の組み合わせの拒否、一覧のスキーマ）。フィルターのモデル（分割、エスケープ、フォルダー、ワイルドカード、include の制約）。実行のモデル（静かなソースでの収束と再実行、途中で止まった実行の続き、コピー後・一覧後の上書き、一覧後のアップロード、全体検証での ERROR、ソースの削除、アーカイブ側での書き込み）。イベントのスキーマと判断、ハンドラーの通知と失敗、遅れの上限、環境変数。2 つのスタックのアサーション
note.en: 63 tests. The plan (new, changed, same; PRESERVE and REMOVE; an empty source listing deleting everything; filtered-out objects not deleted; overwriting a newer archive object and OverwriteMode NEVER; TransferMode ALL; include and exclude; refusing ALL with REMOVE; the listing schema). The filter model (splitting, escapes, folders, wildcards, the include restriction). The execution model (convergence and re-runs on a quiet source, finishing an interrupted execution, overwrites after the copy and after the listing, an upload after the listing, ERROR under whole-dataset verification, deletes in the source, writes made in the archive). The event schema and decision, the handler's notification and failure, the lag bound, the environment. Assertions for both stacks
Type check of src, infra, test, and scripts

summary.ja: 38章の DataSync のタスクを AWS で一度も実行していない。未確認: cdkd 0.296.28 が `AWS::DataSync::LocationS3` と `AWS::DataSync::Task` を Cloud Control API 経由で作れること、`AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy` の作成、大阪リージョンのスタックのデプロイに追加の準備が要るか、ロケーションの作成時にロールの権限が検査されること、別リージョンのロケーションの ARN を持つ Basic モードのタスクが動くこと、スケジュールでの実行、DataSync が何を「変わった」と判定するか（とくにタグだけの変更とマルチパートで書かれたオブジェクト）、実行中にソースが変わったときの結果、フィルターで外したオブジェクトが REMOVE で消えるかどうか、バージョニングを有効にしたアーカイブで削除が削除マーカーになること、EventBridge のイベントの実物の形と SUCCESS・ERROR 以外の状態の綴り、何もコピーしない実行の S3 リクエストの数と料金。
summary.en: The chapter 38 DataSync task has never been run on AWS. Unconfirmed: that cdkd 0.296.28 can create `AWS::DataSync::LocationS3` and `AWS::DataSync::Task` through Cloud Control API; creating `AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy`; whether deploying a stack to the Osaka Region needs extra preparation; that the role is checked when a location is created; that a Basic mode task holding a location ARN from another Region runs; scheduled executions; what DataSync treats as changed (a tag-only change and objects written in parts in particular); the outcome when the source changes during an execution; whether an object a filter excludes is deleted under REMOVE; that a delete in the versioned archive becomes a delete marker; the real shape of the EventBridge event and the spelling of states other than SUCCESS and ERROR; the number and cost of S3 requests in an execution that copies nothing.

resume.ja: `vp run move:infra:deploy` の出力の `SourceLocationArn` を控え、`vp run move:archive:infra:deploy -c sourceLocation=<ARN>` を実行する。本文「デプロイ」の順に、東京のバケットにオブジェクトを置き、`aws datasync start-task-execution --region ap-northeast-3 --task-arn <TaskArn>` で実行して `describe-task-execution` の数を読む。同じ実行をもう一度行い、コピーが 0 件になることと、請求の S3 リクエストを確かめる。最後に `vp run move:empty --yes`、`move:archive:infra:destroy`、`move:infra:destroy`。
resume.en: Note `SourceLocationArn` from `vp run move:infra:deploy`, then run `vp run move:archive:infra:deploy -c sourceLocation=<ARN>`. Following the chapter's deploy page, put objects in the Tokyo bucket, run `aws datasync start-task-execution --region ap-northeast-3 --task-arn <TaskArn>`, and read the counters from `describe-task-execution`. Run it again to see zero copies, and check the S3 requests on the bill. Finish with `vp run move:empty --yes`, `move:archive:infra:destroy`, and `move:infra:destroy`.

summary.ja: アカウントをまたぐコピーを試していない。`-c writerRole=<ARN>` はアーカイブのバケットポリシーに 1 つのステートメントを足すだけで、ソース側のアカウントでのロール、ロケーション、タスクの作成は、この章のスタックに含まれていない。R2 とのあいだのコピー（DataSync の object storage ロケーション、Super Slurper、Sippy）も実行していない。
summary.en: A copy across accounts was not tried. `-c writerRole=<ARN>` only adds one statement to the archive's bucket policy; creating the role, the locations, and the task in the source account is not part of this chapter's stacks. Copies to and from R2 (a DataSync object storage location, Super Slurper, Sippy) were not run either.

resume.ja: DataSync のユーザーガイドの「Transferring data between Amazon S3 buckets across AWS accounts」の手順に沿って、ソース側のアカウントでロールを作り、その ARN を `-c writerRole=` に渡してアーカイブのスタックをデプロイする。ロケーションは `aws datasync create-location-s3` で作る。
resume.en: Follow the DataSync user guide's "Transferring data between Amazon S3 buckets across AWS accounts": create the role in the source account, pass its ARN as `-c writerRole=` when deploying the archive stack, and create the location with `aws datasync create-location-s3`.
